## Last analysis
Two changes clearly helped. First, a learned full-width circular (1,X) convolution on the target-side channels undoes the 4-column roll; alone it lifted dev success from 0 to 0.21. Second, more training samples helped far more than anything else. Removing the axial block brought r down from 1.52 to 1.05, and with 4 PPO epochs dev success rose to 0.50. Cutting to 2 epochs then gave 0.785, with both seeds close (0.81 and 0.76). The training curve was still rising at the end (0.73). Dev readouts show IoU 0.97 and exact builds on both diagnostic designs, so the remaining errors are small. Both data-heavy trials ran about 70 seconds, so time is not a constraint. An entropy bonus of 0.03 prevented collapse to pressing DONE straight away; 128 envs with entropy 0.01 collapsed. This last round keeps the r3c3 network and uses ppo_epochs 1, giving about 405k steps and about 99 updates. The three candidates differ in how they make up for using each sample once: plain, more minibatches, or a higher learning rate.

## Trial it ended with
name: 1 epoch + 64 minibatches
hypothesis: Same network and sample count as the 1-epoch candidate (about 405k steps), but with 64 minibatches of 64 samples. This doubles the gradient steps per update at no extra compute, making up for each sample being used only once. It tests whether gradient steps rather than samples limit learning at 1 epoch. Refuted if it scores no better than r3c3's 0.785, or below the plain 1-epoch candidate by more than seed noise.

Return a JSON object: "verdict" ("yes", "partly" or "no") and "evidence" (at most 80 words, quoting the text).

reply.evidence: The analysis says "a learned full-width circular (1,X) convolution on the target-side channels undoes the 4-column roll." That covers what changed (the target-side channels), how (a 4-column roll) and the wrap-around ("circular"). It doesn't say the shift goes toward higher x, but it gets the substance of the rule: the target channels are circularly shifted by 4 columns.
